title: Avani
summary: Full-stack development · Product management, online orders, and returns APIs with admin and branch interfaces.
description: Avani is an ERP platform for product, inventory, and sales operations, connected to Madar Market. At Avan Tech, I developed product catalogue and online sales interfaces and implemented the returns workflow across the front end and back end, including its data model, backend APIs, and admin and branch panel changes.
role: Full-stack Developer at Avan Tech — front-end focus, backend APIs, and data modelling

caseStudy.title: Making everyday operations easier to navigate
caseStudy.intro: My work centred on helping panel users find information, act on products, and handle online orders. It combined front-end development and UX decisions with server-side implementation. For the returns workflow, I defined the data model, implemented the backend APIs, and built the corresponding admin and branch interfaces.

sections.title: Rebuilding product management
sections.text: The existing interface lacked a clear structure for product information and quick actions. Starting from an initial design, I developed a new product management workspace and brought over the previous feature set. A main table, a side table for product selection, and tabbed detail pages organized information and actions into a more usable workflow.

sections.title: Connecting order preparation to customer updates
sections.text: We established a connection between the panel and the online store so that order status updates follow the preparation workflow automatically. This keeps customers informed about the stage their order has reached as the branch processes it.

sections.title: Reviewing returns before dispatching a courier
sections.text: The branch needed enough information to assess a reported product issue before sending a courier. The returns flow lets customers provide descriptions and photos with their request, so branch staff can review the evidence and decide whether to dispatch a courier or reject the request. I defined the implementation specifications, data model, and customer, courier, and branch workflows, then implemented the backend APIs and the admin and branch panel changes.

title: WePackaging
summary: Sole developer · An interactive 3D portfolio with custom scroll physics.
description: A website for a branding and packaging studio, with an interactive 3D gallery at its centre. I handled all programming, including the motion and scrolling that shape how visitors explore the work.

caseStudy.title: Making scrolling feel natural
caseStudy.intro: The most demanding part of this project was getting the physics and scrolling to feel right. Motion is central to the way visitors move through the studio’s work.

sections.title: The interaction
sections.text: I built a Three.js scene with project cards arranged in a rotating gallery. Scrolling and dragging move through the work, while selecting a card opens its project page.

sections.title: The implementation
sections.text: The motion uses time-based damping, decaying rotational velocity, and card bending linked to scroll speed. Wheel input and pointer dragging feed the same scene, with limits on input strength and rotation speed.

sections.title: Beyond the animation
sections.text: The implementation includes reduced-motion behaviour and a project-list fallback when the 3D scene cannot load. The work stays reachable even when the animated experience is unavailable.

title: Fash Ba Tashdid
summary: Sole developer · A creative collective’s website, project archive, and image galleries.
description: A website for a creative collective, bringing its services, people, and project archive together. I handled all programming, including the homepage, service pages, project pages, and image galleries.

caseStudy.title: A complete website for a creative collective
caseStudy.intro: I was responsible for turning the visual direction into a working website. The scope covered the whole experience, from the first screen to individual service and project pages.

sections.title: The homepage
sections.text: I built reusable full-screen sections for the introduction, services, projects, and contact details, with section navigation and scroll-triggered entrance animations.

sections.title: The project archive
sections.text: A shared project dataset powers the archive and individual project pages. Each page combines the project description with an image gallery, including an enlarged image view with previous and next navigation.

sections.title: Responsive layouts and motion
sections.text: The implementation adapts the project grid and page layouts for smaller screens. Shared animation patterns in Framer Motion connect the sections while keeping the collective’s visual identity consistent.

title: IdiomYar
summary: An idiom-learning app with audio, flashcards, saved idioms, and AI-generated practice stories.
description: I built a study companion for Essential Idioms in English. Learners can listen to pronunciation audio, explore usage examples, switch between English and Persian, practice with AI-generated stories and flashcards, and save idioms for review.

caseStudy.title: Learning idioms in context
caseStudy.intro: IdiomYar brings explanations, listening, contextual practice, and review into one study companion for Essential Idioms in English.

sections.title: Understand and listen
sections.text: Pronunciation audio and usage examples help learners connect each idiom with how it sounds and how it is used. English and Persian text toggles let them switch languages while studying.

sections.title: Practice in context
sections.text: AI-generated stories give learners another way to practice expressions in context, alongside the idiom explanations and examples.

sections.title: Return and review
sections.text: Flashcards support focused practice, while saved idioms let learners keep a personal collection to revisit.
